missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-regular-conditional-laws-C002 (partial): The worked boundary is missing for this entry. def:p15-regular-conditional-law (handbook/parts/p15/regular-conditional-laws.tex lines 49-51) says the regular-conditional-probability special case (S=Omega, target sigma-algebra F_0, X the identity) 'needs an existence hypothesis on the outcome space itself'. That is, it claims a regular conditional law need not exist unless (Omega,F_0) satisfies some hypothesis. Nothing on the handbook route shows this. No probability space and sub-sigma-algebra G are given for which no probability kernel from (Omega,G) to (Omega,F_0) satisfies the defining identities, and no argument for the necessity is written. The only support is the citation at conditioning-independence-and-information-w02b-p15-008.tex lines 235-239. It points to Durrett p. 214 (PDF p. 222), which says such laws do not always exist and credits Dieudonne (1948) without giving the example. That is a citation where a demonstration is owed. The countable-cocountable model (w02b-p15-008 annex lines 171-269) does not fill the gap: it shows a source-sense law that cannot be repaired, but a regular conditional law still exists in that model. Owed: a written model in which no regular conditional probability exists, with its proof, or a written argument that establishes the stated need for a hypothesis.
